policy: Donor files were read at their pinned commit in the local mirror (tools/mirrors.py), as data; nothing was run. Ideas only, in westack's own words; no donor text is copied (skills/westack/provenance/RIGHTS.md). The component classification is skills/westack/provenance/absorption.json (gstack.benchmark.browser-perf).

usefulness_legend.strong: shaped the skill's structure or its numbers
usefulness_legend.useful: added a rule or a check

sources.read: searched, then lines 80-254 (collection, baseline, comparison thresholds, budgets, trend, report)

taken.mechanism: Page metrics read from the browser's own performance entries: navigation timing, paint entries, a buffered largest-contentful-paint observer, and a resource inventory with the slowest resources, scripts and stylesheets.
Repeated runs per page summarized as median and range; a comparison verdict needs runs on both sides and a named limiter, else inconclusive.

Thresholds by unit: timing over 50% or over 500 ms a regression and over 20% a warning; size over 25% and over 10%; request count over 30% a warning; a delta inside either side's spread is no measurable difference.
Budgets (FCP, LCP, JavaScript, CSS, transfer, requests) with fail at the budget, a warning from 90%, and a grade by the share below budget.
Saved runs kept for a trend view.

rejected: The browser daemon and its scripting dialect: westack drives the host's own browser tools (core browser.md).
Writing reports under .gstack/ in the repository: run files go in the evidence folder.
Relying on the gh CLI to find the base branch for page discovery: the user names the pages or the change.
notes: westack adds CLS (a layout-shift observer) and a CLS budget of 0.1, which the donor does not collect, and request and command targets beside pages.

donors.system: gstack benchmark's 'Vet the number' section, itself derived from pstack's benchmark-checklist (Lauren Tan, MIT, per its header and gstack NOTICE.md)
donors.licence: MIT (gstack); the section names pstack (MIT) as its idea source

taken.mechanism: Seven questions that test a performance number before anyone acts on it: the limiter, tuning, physical limits, errors, reproduction with alternating runs, whether it matters end to end, and whether the work happened inside the timed region.
Write the claim to ship before measuring; inconclusive when a difference is claimed without a limiter, a side ran untuned, or the error and did-it-happen questions went unanswered.
taken.where: SKILL.md steps 1-5 and rule 2; scripts/perfcheck.py compare and validate
